name: grid
description: CSS grid with column-count presets and token-bound gap. Pass `cols="auto-fit"` + `minColWidth` for responsive grids without media queries.

props.name: cols
props.description: Number of fixed columns, or `"auto-fit"` for responsive tracks (use with `minColWidth`).

props.name: gap
props.description: Gap between cells, bound to `--gap-*` tokens.

props.name: align
props.description: Cell vertical alignment within their grid row.

props.name: minColWidth
props.description: Min track size for `cols="auto-fit"` (e.g. `"20rem"`). Ignored when `cols` is a fixed integer.

values.description: Single column — items stack vertically inside the grid.
Tracks repeat to fill width, never below `minColWidth`.

variants.name: gap
variants.description: Gap between cells, bound to `--gap-*` tokens.

variants.name: align
variants.description: Cell vertical alignment within their grid row.

values.description: Cells align to top of row.
Cells align to bottom of row.

slots.name: children
slots.description: Grid cells — typically Cards, images, or any uniform block.

examples.title: Responsive auto-fit
examples.description: Tracks fit as many 20rem columns as the viewport allows; no media queries needed.

ai.whenToUse: Use for visually-aligned grids of similar items: card galleries, image walls, dashboard tiles, settings panels. Prefer `cols="auto-fit"` + `minColWidth` over hand-written breakpoints when the column count should adapt to viewport width.
ai.whenNotToUse: Don't use for one-dimensional flows — use `Stack` (vertical) or `Cluster` (horizontal). Don't use for tabular data — use `<table>` or DataTable. Don't fight `Grid` to make uneven columns; if cells need different sizes, use a flexbox layout or a CSS grid with named tracks directly.
commonMistakes: Setting `cols={5}` and getting nothing — the preset only supports 1/2/3/4/6 (deliberate, to avoid odd visual rhythms); use `cols="auto-fit"` for arbitrary counts
Passing `cols="auto-fit"` without `minColWidth` — the default `16rem` may not match your design intent
Using `Grid` for two children when `Cluster` or `Stack` would communicate intent better
ai.accessibilityNotes: Grid is presentational. If the grid renders a list of similar items, wrap in `<ul>`/`<li>` for screen-reader semantics — Grid only handles visual layout.
